IN THE YEAR 2000!
A Future Adventure
Sandbox Software, (C) 1993
Version 1.9
==============================

It's the year 2000! Cars fly.
Robots mow the lawn. Dinner
comes in a pill. The aliens
next door are VERY friendly.
And there's a phone booth on
every single corner, because
every phone booth is a
Teleport-A-Phone now - only 25
cents a call.

Dex Dynamo, age 11, wrote the
greatest science fair report
in the solar system: "THE
POCKET TELEPHONE." Then Sparky
3000, his robot dog, ate it.
The Science Fair is today, at
3:00. On the Moon.

Help Dex find his pages in
seven levels of the future:

1. DOME SWEET DOME: the
   suburbs of Hover Heights
2. THE CLOUD LANE: Grandpa's
   flying CitiCar, nine miles
   to the Skyway
3. THE INFORMATION
   SUPERHIGHWAY: fourteen
   lanes of hover traffic
4. MEGA MALL 2000: the arcade,
   TV-RAMA, and the food court
5. THE TELEPORT-A-PHONE
   EXCHANGE: wrong number!
   (several of them)
6. THE MOON: moon buggies and
   meteor showers
7. THE SCIENCE FAIR: catch
   Sparky before the judges go

REQUIREMENTS
------------
* 286 or better, VGA graphics,
  640K of memory, a hard disk.
* Sound Blaster (or
  compatible) for music and
  digitized sound; the PC
  speaker works too.

To play, copy all the files to
one directory and type
YEAR2000.

CONTROLS
--------
* Arrow keys: walk (joystick
  works too); in Grandpa's
  CitiCar, Left and Right
  steer
* W A S D: walk, same as the
  arrows
* Q / E: walk up-left /
  up-right
* Keypad 7 9 1 3: walk
  diagonally
* Space: fire the Laser-Tag
  Zapper
* F1 help, F2 status
  (quarters!)
* F3 music, F4 sound on/off
* F5 save, F6 load, Esc quit

HINTS
-----
* Phone booths cost a quarter.
  Keep one in your pocket!
* Wait for the laser fences to
  blink off.
* Zapping a car only makes it
  swerve. Save your charge for
  robots.
* In the Teleport-A-Phone
  Exchange, booth number 4 is
  out of order. Try another
  number - you'll get there
  eventually.
* Read the teletype in the
  exchange hall. It knows a
  thing or two.
* Grandpa lost his key ring in
  the hedge garden. His
  CitiCar won't open without
  it.
* Three gates guard the
  CitiCar: all seven pages,
  then the Zapper, then the
  keys. Walk into each one.
* Grandpa's CitiCar likes a
  honk.
* In the Cloud Lane, traffic
  starts as a dot on the
  horizon. Pick a clear lane
  early, and keep right when
  the sign nears 0 MI.
* The judges want 20 pages.
  There are lots more than
  that.
* Came to the fair short? The
  school copier prints more.

-----------------

your friends, upload it to
your favorite BBS, and play it

pages.head: Welcome to the Future!
pages.html:
In The Year 2000!

A Future Adventure from Sandbox Software, 1993.

Everybody knows what the year 2000 will be like. Cars will fly. Robots will mow the lawn, walk the dog and fold the laundry. Dinner will come in a pill (the turkey kind, with stuffing). The aliens will land, and they will be very friendly. And best of all, every phone booth on every corner will be a Teleport-A-Phone: drop in a quarter, dial, and BZZZT! you're across town.

We made a game about it, so you don't have to wait eight whole years.

You are Dex Dynamo, age 11, of 42 Dome Circle, Hover Heights. You wrote the greatest science fair report in the solar system: THE POCKET TELEPHONE - a telephone so small you could carry it in your pocket. (Twenty pages! With diagrams!)

Then Sparky 3000, your robot dog, ate it.

The Science Fair is today at 3:00 PM. It is on the Moon. Get going!

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
What you need

  • An IBM PC or compatible, 286 or faster
  • VGA graphics and 640K of memory
  • A hard disk
  • A Sound Blaster for music and digitized sound (the PC speaker works too)

Installing

Make a directory on your hard disk, for example C:\YEAR2000, copy every file from the disk into it, and type YEAR2000.

The title screen

The intro counts all the way from 1992 to the year 2000 for you. Press any key for the menu, which is on TV, naturally. Choose Play to begin, Read Storyline to see how Sparky ate the report, or Read Instructions for a quick reminder of the controls. Leave the menu alone and Dex will show you around Hover Heights by himself.

Your goal

Collect at least 20 pages of your report across six levels of the future, catch Sparky to get back the cover page, and turn everything in to the judges at the Moon School Science Fair.

pages.head: Controls
pages.html:
Arrow keys or W A S DWalk up, left, down and right (a joystick works too)
Q / EWalk diagonally up-left / up-right
7 9 1 3 on the number padWalk diagonally up-left, up-right, down-left, down-right
Left / Right (or A / D) in Grandpa's CitiCarSteer one lane left or right
SpaceFire the Laser-Tag Zapper (once you have one)
F1Help
F2Status: your score, lives, hit points and how many quarters you have
F3 / F4Music / sound effects on and off
F5 / F6Save / load a game
EscQuit to the menu

Moving around

Pressing two arrows together won't walk you on a slant. That's what Q, E and the number pad's corner keys are for.

Walk into things to use them. Walk into a page to pick it up, into a phone booth door to dial, and into an arcade game to play it. Doors that need a key open by themselves when you have the key.

Glass tubes and moonwalk belts carry you along whether you like it or not - you can step off to the side. On the Moon, your moon suit makes you bound along a whole block at a time.

Flying Grandpa's CitiCar

The CitiCar flies itself: it always heads straight on, and all you do is steer. Each tap of Left or Right moves it one whole lane, and it finishes the move before it takes another.

Tip: nobody can see how many quarters are in their pocket without looking. Press F2!

pages.head: Things of the Future
pages.html:
Report pageSparky chewed them up and spat them all over the future. The judges need 20. There are plenty more than that, so don't worry if you miss a few.
QuarterThe money of the future is the same as the money of the past. A Teleport-A-Phone call costs one quarter. So does an arcade game.
Food pillA complete turkey dinner in one capsule. Restores your hit points.
Laser-Tag ZapperFound in your own backyard. Stuns robots. Comes with a full charge.
BatteryMore charge for the Zapper. Size AA, of course - some things never change.
Hover-ColaThe soft drink of tomorrow. An extra life in every can.
Grandpa's key ringIts clicker opens the garage gate to your backyard, and its keys open his CitiCar.
STAFF ONLY keycardOpens the loading dock at Mega Mall 2000.
Moon PassLets you through the airlock into Moon School.

Phone booths

There's one on every corner. Some say OUT on the door: they're out of order, even the ones that ring and ring (nobody's ever there). The ones without the sign work: walk into the door, it takes your quarter, and the booth fills with sparkles. Step inside to teleport.

pages.head: Friends and Robots
pages.html:
Friendly folks

Aliens live next door now and they love a hug. Walk into one for a hug that heals you, and they'll beam home happy. Grandma in Florida hugs too.

Robots (zappable)

  • Robo-mowers trim the lawns in neat little squares.
  • Robo-dogs want to play fetch. With you.
  • Paperboy-bots and the newspaper cannons deliver the morning news at 60 miles an hour.
  • Fax-bots, security robots, runaway hover carts and robot shoppers crowd the Skyway and the Mall.
  • Telemarketer robots at the phone exchange really want to talk to you about switching your long-distance company.

A robot that chases you short-circuits when it bumps you, but it hurts. Zap them first!

Things that don't stop for anybody

Flying cars (even Grandpa's old CitiCar), fax trucks, hoverboard kids, moon buggies and dinosaurs. A bump hurts once, then they honk and swerve past (or back off) and leave you be. A zap does the same, but it wastes a charge. Meteors just hurt. Get out of the way!

Up in the Cloud Lane the hover cars and fax trucks are all going your way, only slower, so they come back at you out of the distance. A bump costs some hit points (a truck costs more), and they swerve off into the clouds in a puff. The pages and dinner pills drifting down the lanes are yours if you steer into them.

Other dangers

Laser fences blink on and off - walk through while they're off. Tar pits are sticky and hot. And watch the sky on the Moon.

pages.head: The Levels
pages.html:
1. Dome Sweet Dome

Hover Heights, where the domes are white and the lawns are mowed by robots. Grandpa lost his key ring in the hedge garden; the Zapper is in your backyard, behind the garage gate. The phone booths on the corner, by the newspaper cannons, are all out of order today. Grandpa's 1976½ CitiCar is plugged in by your dome: the car of tomorrow since the Bicentennial, one mile of range for every hour on the cord. Give it a honk. Its door has a note on it, KEYS?, and it opens for his key ring: that's your way out.

2. The Cloud Lane

Grandpa's keys open his CitiCar, it unplugs itself, puts out its stubby wings, and up you go: 2,000 feet up, in the driver's seat. It flies itself; you only steer. Hover cars and fax trucks come out of the distance in all three lanes, a dot on the horizon first, and some of your report pages are blowing down the lanes too. The sign counts the miles to the Skyway. At 0 MI the exit ramp opens on the right, so be in the right lane.

3. The Information Superhighway

The CitiCar sets you down on the deck and flies itself home to its charger. Everybody's been talking about it, and here it is: fourteen lanes of hover traffic hauling faxes through the clouds. Cross island by island. Ride the pneumatic tube if you're brave, and catch the latest on the Skyway News Feed along the north rail.

4. Mega Mall 2000

The ARCADE, TV-RAMA and its FOOD court, a hover-rink downstairs, and a loading dock behind the STAFF ONLY door. The keycard is in the laser display case at TV-RAMA.

pages.head: More Levels
pages.html:
5. The Teleport-A-Phone Exchange

Every booth in the world goes through here, and half of them are wrong numbers: Grandma's condo in Florida, the inside of a TV set, the bottom of the sea, the Jurassic period. Every room has quarters, so keep dialing. Booth number 4 is out of order. In the corner, the Restoring the Signal exhibit has a 1916 crank phone (go on, ring it) and a teletype that keeps typing the same tip, with no phone line at all. Somewhere down the line is the Moon Shuttle launch pad: its boarding ramp counts down as you arrive, 6, 5, 4, and opens on GO.

6. The Moon

Moon buggies, the Crater Cafe (dinner in one pill), friendly aliens and an afternoon meteor shower. The Moon Pass is at the Visitor Center at the top of meteor alley; the Moon School airlock is up and to the right.

7. The Science Fair

Sparky is running around the gym with the cover page in his mouth, and the volcano projects are erupting. Zap him three times. Each zap changes his game: first he roams, then he plays keep-away (corner him against a project or a wall), then he gets the zoomies. He never bites, but the lava stings. After the third zap he gets dizzy, then trots over to you and drops the page at your feet. Pick it up, and don't zap it! Then turn in 20 pages at the judges' table, hand over the cover, and step up to the podium. Short of pages? Stand at the copier's tray by the signs: it prints a page every few seconds.

pages.head: Tips from the Future
pages.html:
• Always keep one quarter for the phone booth. Arcade games are fun, but they eat quarters.
  • If you run out of quarters at the phone exchange, every room has more - and they come back each time you dial.
  • Robots that chase you are slower than you are. Lead them around, then zap them.
  • In the Cloud Lane, watch the horizon: everything starts as a dot there. Pick your lane early; a lane change takes a moment, and so does the lane after it.
  • When the sign gets down to 1 MI, get over to the right lane and stay there. The ramp opens at 0.
  • Look both ways on the Superhighway. Trucks are slow; the teal cars are not.
  • Laser fences stay off longer than they stay on. Wait for the click, then go.
  • Pages count across all the levels. You don't need every single one.
  • Careful with the Zapper near the cover page: a zap will burn it up! If that happens, the school keeps one spare cover beside the copier. There is only the one.
  • Friendly aliens are worth a detour when you're hurt.

About this game

In The Year 2000! was made with GAME-MAKER 2.0 by Recreational Software Designs. Design, pictures, music and robot dog: Claude, for Sandbox Software.

items.title: In The Year 2000 Hint Book
items.note: Answers hidden: use the red film
items.intro: Stuck in the future? Find your question, then lay the red film over the answer. Read only the one you need: the Science Fair starts at 3:00 sharp!

hints.a: In your own backyard, north of the garage wall. The clicker on Grandpa's key ring opens the GATE CLICK door first.
In the hedge garden at the bottom left of the neighborhood. Squeeze in through the gaps in the hedges; a robo-mower guards them. The ring opens both the garage gate and the CitiCar.

hints.q: How do I leave the neighborhood?
hints.a: In Grandpa's CitiCar, plugged in by your dome. Its door has a note on it: KEYS? Find his key ring, then walk into the door. (The corner phone booths are all out of order today. Save your quarters for later.)

hints.q: Can I zap the hoverboard kids?
hints.a: No. They zoom up and down the roads, so look both ways and cross behind them.

hints.q: How do I drive this thing?
hints.a: You don't: Grandpa's CitiCar flies itself. Left and Right (or A and D) steer it one whole lane at a time. Up and Down do nothing up here.

Everything comes out of the middle of the horizon as a dot, then slides into its lane. Watch which way the dot drifts, and move as soon as you know. When two lanes are blocked, the third is clear, and often has a page in it.
Watch the sign: SKYWAY 9 MI counts down a mile every six seconds. At 0 MI the exit ramp lights up over the RIGHT lane. Be in the right lane and the car takes the ramp by itself.
Dinner pills come down the lanes too. Steer into one for a turkey dinner.

hints.q: How do I cross fourteen lanes of traffic?
hints.a: Island by island. Wait on a deck for a gap, then dash. Gold trucks are slow, red cars are medium, and the teal cars are VERY fast.
At the far right of the last platform at the bottom, past the FAX-A-PIZZA billboard. The one next to where you start is out of order.

hints.q: What does the glass tube do?
hints.a: It whisks you along to the right in a hurry. Step off the side if you want to grab a page instead.

hints.q: How do I get the STAFF ONLY keycard?
hints.a: It's in the corner of TV-RAMA behind a laser fence. Stand next to the lasers and walk through as soon as they blink off. They stay off three times longer than they stay on.

hints.q: Where is the STAFF ONLY door?
hints.a: On the south wall of the concourse, on the right. The loading dock behind it has three more laser fences and the phone booth.

hints.q: Are the arcade games worth it?
hints.a: Arcade games give 1,000 points and pinball gives 2,500, but each one eats a quarter and then it's GAME OVER. Never spend your last quarter!

hints.q: The security robots keep catching me.
hints.a: They are slower than you are. Lead them in a loop, then turn around and zap them.

Booth 3 is the shortest way: inside a TV set, then the Jurassic period, then the Moon Shuttle launch pad. Booths 1 and 2 work too, they just take the scenic route. (The teletype in the corner has been trying to tell you.)
Every room has quarters, and they come back every time you dial into it. Pick them up before you dial again.

hints.q: How do I get on the Moon Shuttle?
hints.a: Walk up the boarding ramp right under the rocket. It's chained off while the countdown runs (6, 5, 4...): wait for its board to say GO. The booth on the launch pad only takes you back to the hall.
Booth 1 goes to Grandma's condo in Florida. She gives a big hug that heals you.
At the top left of the Moon, west of the big dome. Hop up meteor alley to get it.

hints.q: How do I dodge the meteors?
hints.a: They fall at a slant from the sky along the top edge. Watch where they land, then hop through behind them.
The base at the top right. Walk into the MOON PASS airlock with the pass, and the door to the Science Fair is inside.
Zap him three times. Each zap changes his game: he roams, then plays keep-away (corner him), then gets the zoomies. Then he gets dizzy and drops the cover page.

You zapped it. A zap burns the cover page up, so stop firing once Sparky drops it. The school keeps one spare cover, on the floor right beside the copier at the bottom of the gym: walk into it. There is only the one.

hints.q: What do I do at the judges' table?
hints.a: Walk into the table with 20 pages to turn them in, then walk into the COVER table behind it with the cover page. Then step up to the podium!
The lava blobs wander slowly. Keep moving, and grab a food pill if you get singed.

hints.q: What's in the closet next to the launch pad?
hints.a: Some say the felt-maker left something behind. In the future not every brick is a brick.
It doesn't need one. Look along the Moon Shuttle pad's right wall for a brick with teal light glowing through its mortar.

On the Moon Shuttle pad, get into the row of the boarding ramp, on the ramp's right side (don't step on the ramp itself, or you're off to the Moon). Walk right into the glowing brick: you walk straight through it. Press G to pick up the felt egg, then walk on into the rocket hatch at the far end.

items.title: The Hover Heights Herald
items.headline: IT'S THE YEAR 2000!
items.deck: Cars fly, robots mow, dinner fits in a pill; local robot dog eats science report

photo.caption: The Dynamo family dome on Dome Circle. Robots mowed this lawn.

columns: HOVER HEIGHTS - The new millennium arrived right on time last night, and so did everything else. Flying cars filled the Information Superhighway by breakfast. Robo-mowers trimmed every lawn in neat little squares.

Dinner, as everybody always said it would, now comes in a pill. "It tastes just like turkey," said one diner. "With stuffing."

The aliens next door report that they are having a lovely time and would like a hug.

One family was not celebrating. Sparky 3000, a robot dog, reportedly ate a twenty-page science report titled The Pocket Telephone. "A telephone in your POCKET?" laughed one neighbor. "What'll they think of next?"
briefs: Computers everywhere woke up fine. The only bug in Hover Heights was a robot dog.
Still 25 cents a call. Booth 4 at the exchange is out of order again.
Sunny. Meteor showers this afternoon. Bring a helmet.

items.title: The wrong-number die (fold your own)
items.note: A square of paper that blows up into a die
items.heading: The Wrong-Number Die
items.intro: Cut out the square, fold it and blow it up into a six-sided die for choosing which booth to dial in the Exchange. Nothing about it is right: its faces are 1, 2, 3, a 4 that is out of order, a 7 (there is no booth 7) and a 0, which is the hole you blow in. Opposite faces add up to 4, 6 and 7. Roll it, then dial whatever it says.
items.foot: If you roll the 4, the booth is out of order. Roll again.

news.head: Our second game: In The Year 2000!
news.html: Sandbox Software is four months old, and its second game is in your hands. In In The Year 2000! you are Dex Dynamo, age 11, and your robot dog Sparky 3000 just ate your science report. Find 20 pages across six levels of the future, from the dome homes of Hover Heights to the Moon, and get them to the Science Fair by 3:00. Bring a quarter: every phone booth is a Teleport-A-Phone.

news.head: What will the year 2000 be like?
news.html: We asked our classmates what they expect in seven short years. The top answers: flying cars (41 votes), robot dogs (29), dinner in a pill (17), and a telephone small enough to fit in your pocket (2 votes, and one of those was a joke). Our programmer is betting on the pocket telephone. Our mail room is still betting on the mail.

news.head: Sparky says thanks
news.html: Register In The Year 2000! for $12 and you get the next Sandbox Software game on a 3 1/2" disk, a printed manual and a sticker for your computer. Sparky promises not to eat any of it.

news.head: Since last issue: Snowbound, rough edges and all
news.html: Snowbound got our roughest reviews and our warmest letters. Yes, it’s the simplest game we’ll ever make; it’s also the truest. Readers from all over Mineral County wrote to say we got the sled run on Jamie Street just right. The most-asked question: does the arcade eat all your dollars? Only if you let it. Count the can (F2) before you head for the register.

news.head: Around the Sandbox: Homework comes first
news.html: The founder is a junior at Frankfort High, so Sandbox Software keeps strict hours: after homework, before bed, and all day Saturday. The office is still a desk, the family 286 and a stack of graph paper. The snow shovel has moved to the porch. It may be needed again.

news.head: In the workshop: A puzzle made of pure Game-Maker
news.html: The founder's notebook is already full. First on the list is a puzzle game where electricity is made of ordinary Game-Maker blocks and monsters: switches, fuses, and a little robot who must never touch a live wire. Its working title is Ohm Sweet Ohm, and we apologize for it now. It won’t be quick: there’s homework first, and a diploma after that.

news.head: Letters: "Did you make it to the mall?"
news.html:
"In Snowbound, did the real founder make it to the register in time?" - A reader in West Virginia

The Scoop replies: Look at the name on this newsletter. Then look at the box your game came in.
